title: Machine learning forecasts prehospital transfusion needs in trauma across registries
summary: Models trained on 364,350 patients in the US National Trauma Data Bank used vital signs, injury patterns and anticoagulant medication to predict prehospital transfusion, and were externally validated on 54,210 patients from three registries in Europe and Canada. External AUROC was 0.87 (0.86-0.87) for any transfusion and 0.88 for packed red blood cells, and the high-probability group had higher mortality and haemorrhagic death. The study is retrospective registry-based and no prospective test is reported.
ai_technology: Machine learning classifiers, a multiclass model and a regressor on prehospital trauma data

evidence.tested: External validation on three trauma registries covering Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Ireland and Canada.
evidence.unknown: Prospective, real-time prehospital performance and effect on outcomes; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning predicted blood product need from routine prehospital data.
